sources.citation: Leiden University Student Repository record (Primo VE / Alma) for Mulder 2021, incl. Alma IIIF manifest
sources.note: Catalogue record only (abstract, open-access flag, handle); used to obtain the PDF.

Nothing on stress. States the languages are known only from South Cushitic loanwords in Dawida and Saghala plus oral tradition; cites Ehret & Nurse 1981, Nurse's paper in Bechhaus-Gerst & Serzisko (eds.) 1988 Cushitic-Omotic pp. 95, 99, Ehret 2010 pp. 203-204, Nurse & Hinnebusch 1993 p. 333, Merritt 1975 (history PhD).

sources.citation: Beer, Samuel J., Andrew Harvey, Maarten Mous, Christian J. Rapold, Terrill Schrock & Ahmed Sosal. 2025. Lateral obstruents in East Africa from an areal and historical perspective: a case for contact-induced non-change. In Language Contact: An International Handbook, vol. 2, 9-22. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9783110443011-002. (Author draft, 16 pp., posted by LHEAf 2023.)
sources.note: Segmental only: inventory of lateral obstruents in Davida Weruga/Mbale and Saghala, derivation of Davida [ɮj]/[ɮ] from Bantu spirantization (Slavikova 1975; Nurse & Hinnebusch 1993), Saghala ɬ attributed to Taita Cushitic loans. No mention of tone, accent, stress or pitch (0 a full-text search for stress/accent hits).

sources.citation: Elderkin, Edward D., Maarten Mous, Derek Nurse, Gerard Philippson, Christian Rapold, Sjef van Lier, Bonny Sands, Ahmed Sosal & Mauro Tosco. 2024. Cushitic in the mountains of Taita, Pare, Kilimanjaro from loan word evidence. Presentation, LHEAf final conference 'Unravelling East Africa's Early Linguistic History', Leiden, 6-8 June 2024. 34 slides (PDF posted by LHEAf, July 2024).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent, tone or pitch (0 hits for tone/tonal/stress/accent/pitch/prosod- in the 34 slides). Taita content is segmental and etymological: Saghala loan-adaptation rules (ħ, ʕ > h or zero; loss of r in C3/intervocalic; loss of ʔ ʕ in C3; voicing of stops; SC ɬ kept as ɬ or > r; ts' > ts; tɬ' > 'tly'; loss of nasal before voiceless fricative), a table of loan layers in Taita Bantu (Taita South Cushitic 11, T SC isolated 6, Early East African 3, Dahalo 12, Coastal/Somali 17, Oromo 3, Maasai 5, other 2) and worked etymologies (gafa 'beard', dah- 'knock', baha 'big', sare 'name',…

sources.citation: Mous, Maarten. 2024. The History of South Cushitic. Conference presentation, 2nd Hybrid Meeting on Cushitic Languages and Linguistics, Naples, 6 December 2024. 28 slides. Leiden: LHEAf project ('Unravelling East Africa's Early Linguistic History').
sources.note: No phonology content for Taita Cushitic: reports the LHEAf 'Taita team' (Nurse, Sands, Tosco, Elderkin, Sosal, Rapold, van Lier, Philippson, Mous) re-etymologising non-Bantu vocabulary in Saghala, Davida, Chaga, Pare; counts of transfers; concludes TC is one of a 'cloud of shadows of Cushitic languages' whose genealogy is 'difficult to impossible to determine'. Zero mentions of tone, accent, stress or pitch anywhere in the slides.

sources.citation: Mous, Maarten. 2023. The classification of South Cushitic. Conference presentation, ICHL26, Heidelberg, 8 September 2023. 51 slides. Leiden: LHEAf project.
sources.note: Nothing on Taita Cushitic phonology; no tone/stress terms in the slides.

sources.citation: Mulder, Sophie. 2021. The Taita Cushites revisited. BA thesis (Descriptive Linguistics), Leiden University (supervisor M. Mous). 68 pp.https://hdl.handle.net/1887/3606925
sources.note: Nothing. The thesis re-examines 41 putative Southern Cushitic loanwords in Saghala/Dawida and Ehret & Nurse's segmental 'sound laws' (ch. 4-5, appendices); no section on phonology, tone, accent or stress of Taita Cushitic. The only prosodic remark is 'loss of final high tone' inside a quoted Iraqw/West-Rift reconstruction (p. 45 = printed p. 44, Appendix 4). Conclusion (p. 16): 'there is too little evidence to prove there are two extinct Taita Cushitic languages.. enough evidence to say there has been Southern Cushitic influence in Saghala'; and (p. 16) 'For making claims about the specific a…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid tait1247 'Cushitic Taita' (Hammarström et al.), with reference records 665703 and 139080
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Lists only two most-extensive descriptions, both of type 'a wordlist or less': Mulder 2021 (listed by Glottolog as a comparative study;minimal) and Ehret & Nurse 1981 (listed by Glottolog as an overview;comparative); status extinct; no grammar, sketch, or phonology exists in the bibliography.
